hadith_en: Salim narrated: "Ibn `Umar used to offer the Maghrib and `Isha' prayers together in Al-Muzdalifa." Salim said, "Ibn `Umar delayed the Maghrib prayer because at that time he heard the news of the death of his wife Safiyah bint Abi `Ubaid. I said to him, 'The prayer (is due).' He said, 'Go on.' Again, I said, 'The prayer (is due).' He said, 'Go on,' till we covered two or three miles. Then he got down, prayed, and said, 'I saw the Prophet ﷺ praying in this way, whenever he was in a hurry during the journey.' `Abdullah (bin `Umar) added, "Whenever the Prophet ﷺ was in a hurry, he used to delay the Maghrib prayer and then offer three units (of the Maghrib) and perform Tasleem, and after waiting for a short while, Iqama used to be pronounced for the `Ishaa' prayer when he would offer two units (i.e., shortened Ishaa prayer) and perform Tasleem. He would never offer any optional prayer till the middle of the night (when he used to pray the Tahajjud).".
syarah_en: ʿAbdullah ibn ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with them) always endeavoured and strived to follow the [example] of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in everything and would always be eager in applying everything that the Prophet ﷺ did at home or [when] traveling.In this hadeeth, the taabiʿeeSaalim ibn ʿAbdullah ibn ʿUmar reports that his father, ʿAbdullah(may Allah be pleased with him) used to combine the Maghrib and ʿIshaa’ prayers at Muzdalifah - which is a place near Makkah between the valley of Muhassir and the two ma’zimayn [i.e., the two mountains of Quzah and ʿArafaat].  which is one of the religious sites which the pilgrims stay at during the Hajj and hasten to after staying at Mount ʿArafaat on the ninth of DhulHijjah, where they pray [both] Maghrib and ʿIshaa’ shortened and combined during this time. Saalim said: Ibn ʿUmar delayed the Maghrib prayer until the time for ʿIshaa’ entered.  This was generally not his habit; rather, he would diligently pray [each] prayer within its respective time. However, the reason for occurring in this instance was because he was informed of the death of his wife, Safiyyah bint AbeeʿUbayd, the sister of al-Mukhtaar al-Thaqafi. The Arabic word used to describe how he was informed is (istasrikha) which refers to the case when one appeals for help with an elevated voice. This happened while Ibn ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with them) was on his way towards Makkah outside of al-Madeenah, so he was hastening to arrive there [as fast as possible].  Then, Saalim notified him that the time of the prayer had arrived, but then ʿAbdullah(may Allah be pleased with him) asked him to carry on with the journey. So, Saalim went away, but later, he reminded him again of the prayer by saying: “The prayer” [as a reminder].  Then, ʿAbdullah responded: “Go on”, until they had travelled two or three miles.  A mile is about one and a half kilometres (1.5 km) approximately. Then, he descended [from his mount] and performed the prayer, while combining Maghrib and ʿIshaa’.  Then he said [to his son]: ‘This was the way I saw the Prophet ﷺ pray whenever he was in a hurry during the journey.’  Meaning: when he needed to hasten during his travels.ʿAbdullah said: ‘I saw that whenever the Prophet ﷺ was hastening to complete his journey, he delayed the Maghrib prayer, then would perform three units - because Maghrib is not shortened - then would perform the tasleem to conclude the prayer; and hardly remained therein - meaning he ﷺ only waited a little while - until [the time for] ʿIshaa’ came in; then he performed the prayer, shortening it to two prayer units. Thereafter, he performed the tasleem and did not perform any supererogatory prayers after ʿIshaa’.  Rather, he slept until he rose out of fear [that he would lose] the night, and then perform tahajjud – as much as Allah willed.There are two ways to join between two consecutive prayers, depending on what is easier at the time and situation at hand:First - Combining by bringing the [second] prayer forward: It is to perform the ʿAsr prayer with Dhuhr, during the time of afternoon prayer (Dhuhr), and ʿIshaa’ with Maghrib during the time for the sunset prayer (Maghrib).Second - Combining by delaying the [first] prayer: and it is to perform the Dhuhr prayer with ʿAsr, during the time of the mid-afternoon prayer (ʿAsr), and Maghrib with ʿIshaa’, during the time for the night prayer (ʿIshaa’).This is all with shortening the prayers with four units to two while traveling.  So, the prayer is shortened and combined, while Maghrib is not shortened, and Fajr is performed separately, and is not joined with any of the others. Likewise, there is no joining between ʿAsr and Maghrib.  And whoever combines two prayers, it is necessary for him to not have a long period of time separating the performance of the two prayers, respectively.  If there is a long separation between the two, he does not join them, and must pray the [second] prayer during its own time.Some of the other benefits that we can conclude from this hadeeth is knowing the virtues of performing night prayers and learning that that the Prophet ﷺ did not omit it at any time, whether when he was at home or traveling.We understand the permissibility in combining Maghrib and ʿIshaa’ while traveling, and that the sunset prayer is not shortened while traveling.Lastly, we learn from this hadeeth that we should observe [and perform] the prayer during its time if there is no [valid] excuse to delay it..
